meta.title: Advanced English Grammar Test (C1-C2) - Combined Topics
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering advanced English grammar topics, combining at least two or more advanced concepts per question.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined C1-C2 level grammar structures such as inversion with conditionals, subjunctive with cleft sentences, and more.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This sentence combines negative adverbial inversion ('Hardly had...') with a mixed conditional. The 'if' clause refers to a past unreal condition, requiring the past perfect ('had consulted'), and the main clause refers to a past unreal result, requiring 'would have been'.
explanation.concept: Negative inversion with past unreal conditions
explanation.formula: Hardly + had + subject + past participle ... would have + past participle + if + subject + had + past participle
examples: Hardly had they arrived when they realized it would have been better if they had prepared.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: It is imperative that it _____ the lead investigator who _____ the final report.

explanation.text: This combines the mandative subjunctive ('it is imperative that it be') with a cleft sentence. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the singular 'investigator', so the verb must be 'signs'.
explanation.concept: Mandative subjunctive in it-clefts
explanation.formula: It is imperative that + subject + base verb + who/that + singular verb
examples: It is essential that it be the manager who approves the budget.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This sentence combines a perfect passive participle clause ('Having been warned') with an advanced passive reporting structure ('is believed to have been'). 'Prior' must be followed by 'to'.
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participles and passive reporting verbs
explanation.formula: Having been + past participle, subject + is believed + to have been + past participle
examples: Having been warned about the risks, the project is believed to have been canceled.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By next year, she will have been managing the department for a decade, so she _____ a vast amount of industry insight.

explanation.text: This combines the future perfect continuous ('will have been managing') with a modal verb of deduction about the past/present ('must have accumulated'), indicating a strong logical conclusion based on the duration of her work.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect Continuous + Modal Verbs of Deduction
explanation.concept: Duration up to a future point leading to past/present deduction
explanation.formula: Subject + will have been + verb-ing + for + time, so + subject + must have + past participle
examples: He will have been working there for years, so he must have learned the system.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a reduced relative clause (past participle 'selected' for passive meaning) with a gerund pattern after 'regret' ('having postponed' for a past action).
explanation.topic: Reduced Relative Clauses + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Past participle reduction and gerund after regret
explanation.formula: Noun + past participle + verb + having + past participle
examples: The documents signed yesterday regret having contained errors.

data.hint: Choose the correct words to complete the elliptical sentence with a discourse marker.
data.question: Although _____ straightforward, the task was, _____, fraught with hidden complexities.

explanation.text: This combines ellipsis in an adverbial clause of concession ('Although seemingly' omits 'it was') with a formal discourse marker of contrast ('nevertheless').
explanation.concept: Omission in adverbial clauses and contrast markers
explanation.formula: Although + (subject + be) + adjective, clause, nevertheless, clause
examples: Although (it was) difficult, the mission was, nevertheless, successful.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a noun clause acting as the subject ('What makes...') requiring a singular verb ('is'), with a double comparative structure ('the more... the less...'). 'We' takes the base verb 'analyze'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in noun clauses and double comparatives
explanation.formula: What + singular verb + is + that + the + comparative + subject + base verb, the + comparative + subject + verb
examples: What is important is that the harder you try, the better you get.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The committee is looking forward to _____ the investigation, despite the management insisting on _____ it off.

explanation.text: This combines verb patterns requiring a gerund after a preposition ('looking forward to' + gerund, 'insisting on' + gerund) with separable phrasal verbs ('carry out', 'put off').
explanation.concept: Preposition + gerund and phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Verb + preposition + gerund + phrasal verb
examples: I look forward to meeting them, despite them putting the meeting off.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines adjective + preposition collocations ('oblivious to', 'ill-equipped') with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it takes 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Adjective collocations and indefinite articles before consonant sounds
explanation.formula: Adjective + to + noun phrase + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: She was oblivious to the fact that it was a unique chance, leaving her ill-equipped.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to ensure subject-verb agreement.
data.question: Neither of the proposed solutions _____ effective, although a number of alternatives _____ under consideration.

explanation.text: This combines quantifiers with subject-verb agreement rules. 'Neither of' takes a singular verb ('has proven'), while 'a number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb ('remain').
explanation.concept: Singular vs. plural verbs with specific quantifiers
explanation.formula: Neither of + plural noun + singular verb; A number of + plural noun + plural verb
examples: Neither of the options is viable, but a number of ideas are being discussed.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'If only' for past regret (requiring past perfect 'had acted') with 'It's high time' for present urgency (requiring past simple 'implemented').
explanation.topic: Wish / If Only + It's High Time
explanation.concept: Past regret and present urgency structures
explanation.formula: If only + subject + past perfect; It is high time + subject + past simple
examples: If only I had known; it is high time we left.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: He behaves as though he _____ the sole owner, and so arrogant _____ his demeanor that colleagues avoid him.

explanation.text: This combines an unreal comparison using 'as though' (requiring past subjunctive 'were') with 'so + adjective' inversion ('so arrogant is his demeanor').
explanation.topic: As Though / As If + So / Such Inversion
explanation.concept: Unreal comparisons and emphatic inversion
explanation.formula: Subject + verb + as though + subject + past subjunctive, and so + adjective + be + subject
examples: She acts as though she knew everything, and so confident is she that no one argues.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines third conditional inversion ('Had the merger been') with 'not only... but also' inversion ('not only would the company... but it would also...').
explanation.topic: Conditional Inversion + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Inversion in conditionals and correlative conjunctions
explanation.formula: Had + subject + past participle, not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + subject + also + verb
examples: Had I known, not only would I have helped, but I would also have stayed.

data.hint: Choose the correct inverted structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Little _____ that under no circumstances _____ the suspect voluntarily surrender.

C.text: did he know / the suspect would

explanation.text: This combines two negative adverbial inversions. 'Little' at the beginning of a clause requires 'did he know', and 'under no circumstances' requires the auxiliary 'would' to precede the subject 'the suspect'.
explanation.topic: Little Did He Know + Under No Circumstances
explanation.concept: Double negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Little + auxiliary + subject + verb + that + under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + verb
examples: Little did they know that under no circumstances would he agree.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines first conditional inversion ('Should you need') with second conditional inversion ('were I to explain'). Both require the base form of the verb after the inverted auxiliary or 'to'.
explanation.topic: Should You Need + Were I To
explanation.concept: Conditional inversion for future possibility and hypothetical situations
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, were + subject + to + base verb, subject + would + base verb
examples: Should you require help, were I to assist, I would be glad.

data.hint: Choose the correct structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the document, bearing the CEO's signature, that _____ the transaction.

explanation.text: This combines an it-cleft sentence ('It was the document... that authorized') with a present participle clause acting as a reduced relative clause ('bearing the CEO's signature').
explanation.concept: Emphasis using it-clefts and present participle reduction
explanation.formula: It + was + noun + , + present participle + , + that + past tense verb
examples: It was the letter, containing the truth, that changed everything.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a mixed conditional (past condition, present result) with the mandative subjunctive. After 'insisted that', the verb must be in the base form ('be'), regardless of the subject 'the team'.
explanation.concept: Past unreal condition with present result and mandative subjunctive
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + past participle + that + subject + base verb, subject + would + base verb
examples: If he had demanded that she be present, we would not be waiting now.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the relative clause.
data.question: The artifacts, which _____ to have been crafted in the 12th century, were recently discovered.

explanation.text: This combines a non-defining relative clause ('which are thought') with an advanced passive reporting structure ('to have been crafted').
explanation.concept: Passive reporting verbs in non-defining relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun, which + is/are + thought/said/believed + to have been + past participle, + main verb
examples: The ruins, which are believed to have been built by Romans, were found.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines modal verbs of deduction about the past ('must have', 'can't have') with gerund patterns. 'Regret' and 'enjoy' are both followed by a gerund ('making', 'facing') when referring to the action itself.
explanation.topic: Modal Verbs of Deduction + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Past deduction and verb patterns requiring gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + must/can't + have + verb + gerund
examples: He must have regretted quitting, as he can't have enjoyed being unemployed.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the comparative sentence.
data.question: The more complex the issue, _____ to resolve.

explanation.text: This combines the double comparative structure ('the more... the harder...') with standard word order (no inversion in the second clause), though ellipsis of 'it is' is also possible in informal contexts, 'it is' is the grammatically complete form.
explanation.concept: Double comparatives with standard or elliptical word order
explanation.formula: The + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb
examples: The sooner we start, the earlier we will finish.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines a discourse marker ('therefore') with noun clauses. The subject clause 'what we need' is singular, so it requires the singular verb 'is', not 'are'. 'Need' must agree with 'we'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in noun clauses with discourse markers
explanation.formula: Whatever + clause, discourse marker, it is evident that + what + subject + base verb + is + singular noun
examples: Whoever they are, however, it is clear that what matters is the result.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: She is accustomed to _____ with clients who are prone to _____ their minds at the last minute.

explanation.text: This combines verb patterns where 'to' functions as a preposition ('accustomed to' + gerund) with an adjective + preposition collocation ('prone to' + gerund).
explanation.concept: Preposition + gerund patterns
explanation.formula: Subject + be + accustomed to + gerund + who + be + prone to + gerund
examples: He is used to working late, and he is prone to making mistakes when tired.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines quantifiers ('very few of' for countable, 'little of' for uncountable) with a phrasal verb ('lived up to'). 'Feedback' is uncountable, so it requires the singular verb 'was'.
explanation.concept: Countable/uncountable quantifiers and phrasal verb usage
explanation.formula: Few of + plural countable noun + phrasal verb, and little of + uncountable noun + singular verb
examples: Little of the advice was useful, and few of the suggestions lived up to expectations.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I wish the majority of the staff _____ more cooperative, but the number of complaints _____ to rise.

explanation.text: This combines 'wish' + past subjunctive for present unreal situations ('were' for the plural 'staff') with subject-verb agreement rules ('the number of' takes a singular verb 'continues').
explanation.concept: Past subjunctive after wish and singular verbs with 'the number of'
explanation.formula: I wish + plural subject + were, but the number of + plural noun + singular verb
examples: I wish the students were quieter, but the number of disruptions continues.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'It's high time' + past simple ('stopped') for present urgency with 'as though' + past subjunctive ('knew') for an unreal comparison.
explanation.topic: It's High Time + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Past simple for present urgency and past subjunctive for unreal comparisons
explanation.formula: It is high time + subject + past simple + as though + subject + past simple
examples: It is high time he stopped behaving as though he owned the place.

data.hint: Choose the correct words to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: _____ critical was the situation that _____ we not intervened, the entire operation would have collapsed.

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective' inversion ('So critical was') with third conditional inversion ('had we not intervened'). 'Such' is used with nouns, while 'so' is used with adjectives.
explanation.concept: Emphatic inversion and conditional inversion
explanation.formula: So + adjective + be + subject + that + had + subject + not + past participle, subject + would have + past participle
examples: So dangerous was the path that had we not been careful, we would have fallen.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines 'not only' inversion ('Not only did the CEO resign') with 'little' inversion ('little did the public know'). Both negative adverbials at the start of a clause require subject-auxiliary inversion.
explanation.topic: Not Only ... But Also + Little Did He Know
explanation.concept: Double negative adverbial inversion
explanation.formula: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but + little + auxiliary + subject + verb
examples: Not only did she win, but little did anyone know she was injured.

data.hint: Choose the correct inverted structures to complete the sentence.
data.question: Under no circumstances _____ disclose the password, _____ to access the system remotely.

C.text: should you / if you will need

D.text: you should / if you will need

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion ('Under no circumstances should you') with first conditional inversion ('should you need'). Both require the auxiliary verb to precede the subject.
explanation.topic: Under No Circumstances + Should You Need
explanation.concept: Negative inversion and conditional inversion
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + base verb, should + subject + base verb
examples: Under no circumstances should you open this, should you value your safety.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines second conditional inversion ('Were I to choose') with an it-cleft sentence ('it would be the second option that I would select'). 'Were I to' must be followed by the base verb, and the relative clause requires 'would select'.
explanation.concept: Conditional inversion and emphasis using it-clefts
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, it would be + noun + that + subject + would + base verb
examples: Were I to decide, it would be this path that I would take.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the mixed conditional passive sentence.
data.question: If the data _____ mishandled, the report _____ considered reliable by now.

C.text: had not been / would have been

explanation.text: This combines a mixed conditional (third conditional 'if' clause for a past unreal condition + second conditional main clause for a present unreal result) with advanced passive structures ('had not been mishandled', 'would be considered').
explanation.concept: Past unreal condition with present result in passive voice
explanation.formula: If + subject + had + not + been + past participle, subject + would + be + past participle
examples: If the letter had not been lost, we would be informed by now.
